summary: Intermittent 429s for mixed real-time and bulk traffic during short burst waves — rate-distribution diagnostic request
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses across a mix of realtime chat traffic and background bulk embedding imports. Throttles appear as short waves (~30s–90s) correlated with their nightly batch job start, but also spike during unrelated realtime traffic peaks. The customer is on a Dedicated pool and expecting predictable throughput; 429s are impacting their user-facing chat latency and causing retries in the ingest pipeline.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat requests see 5–12% 429 rate during bursts, causing perceptible errors to users.
- Background embed import jobs fail and retry; overall backlog grows.
- Business impact: degraded user experience for end customers and risk of missed SLAs for dedicated contract.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id d-pool-78
- Region: us-west-2 (prod-us-west)
- Client: mixed HTTP/1.1 long-lived connections for chat, scheduled worker fleet for batch ingest
- Models in use: open-llama-3b pinned, redwood-opt-1.3b fallback

Observed behavior / constraints:
- 429s show up on both chat route (/v1/chat) and embedding route (/v1/embeddings) roughly during the same short time window.
- Console shows token-consumption spike and transient per-tenant quota exhaustion for ~45s.
- Customer's batch job schedules at 02:00 UTC and is retrying on 429s with exponential backoff; retries are jittered but still overlap with realtime peaks.

Primary ask:
- Request Redwood support to run rate-distribution diagnostics and advise configuration changes (burst pool split, refill windows, route isolation) and confirm whether any server-side accounting mis-attribution (e.g., healthchecks, probes, or proxy keepalives) is contributing to the tenant token depletion.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On customer's dedicated pool, kick off their nightly batch ingest (schedule provided).
2) During an active realtime chat load (10–50 concurrent long-lived sessions), monitor /v1/chat and /v1/embeddings for 429 responses.
3) Observe console token burn and rate-limit headers on rejected responses (x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset).
4) Reproduce locally by replaying captured traffic profile if needed (customer provided HAR + batch job schedule).
logs:
Customer supplied logs (sanitized):
- chat_request_log excerpt: 2026-03-09T02:00:12Z POST /v1/chat 429 x-rate-limit-remaining:0 x-rate-limit-reset:45
- embed_worker log: 2026-03-09T02:00:15Z bulk-upload chunk #12 -> 429; retry queued
- Console snapshot: token_consumption_graph: spike to 1.8x baseline between 02:00:10–02:01:00
- Edge proxy (customer side) shows many keepalives; IP pooling: yes
(Full logs uploaded to ticket attachments.)
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support engineer (A. Patel):
- Verified customer is hitting tenant-level quota exhaustion (token bucket drained).
- Confirmed both realtime and batch routes are counted against the same tenant token pool.
- No recent plan or quota change recorded in billing logs.
- Observed odd small spikes of internal healthcheck traffic from sidecar proxies during same window; need SRE confirmation if healthchecks are charged to tenant on Dedicated.

SRE hypothesis (pending):
- The batch job's parallelism causes many simultaneous start requests that consume tokens at startup (model load/priming or prefix payloads).
- Long-lived chat connections are continuing to consume per-second tokens; combined with the batch start burst they exceed refill rate leading to short-window 429s.
- Possible contribution from edge proxy reusing pooled IPs causing double-counting in edge counting.

Immediate data requests made to infra team:
- Request per-route token accounting for pool d-pool-78 for 2026-03-09 01:59–02:02 UTC (requested via internal S3 report job).
- Check rate-limiter logs for healthcheck and readiness-probe accounting around the burst windows.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel (Support): Reached out to customer for exact batch job manifest and concurrency. Asked for HAR and timing — customer uploaded schedule + worker config (concurrency=48).

2026-03-11 Marco Gutierrez (SRE): Pulled rate-limiter trace; found ~40 simultaneous embedding chunk requests at 02:00:12 UTC that correlate with customer worker startup. Also saw 200 small health-checks (~300ms) from sidecar per node — investigating whether these are counted. Linked internal runbook: confluence.redwood.internal/Runbooks/dedicated-counting

2026-03-11 Priya Menon (Serving Runtime): Observed that model warmup calls include a small metadata payload that consumes ~5 tokens per init call. With 48 workers starting in parallel that is non-negligible. Proposed staggered worker startup or client-side warmup suppression as mitigation.

2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Scheduled a short diagnostic window with customer for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC to capture high-resolution traces. Suggested temporary config: reduce batch worker startup concurrency to 8 and enable route isolation for embeddings to a separate burst pool (if customer wants).
next_steps:
- Run requested per-route token accounting report and attach CSV.
- Confirm whether healthchecks are charged on Dedicated; if yes, identify nodes and propose exempting internal readiness probes from tenant accounting.
- Run scheduled diagnostic session with customer 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.
- Provide configuration change recommendations: staggered worker startup, split embedding route into isolated burst lane (priority pool), or increase dedicated pool refill/burst credits temporarily.
- Follow up with a concise config playbook for customer's engineering team.
sla_notes: First response met on 2026-03-11. SLA due 2026-03-12 (P1). Diagnostic session scheduled before SLA expiry; customer agreed to temporary mitigation (lower startup concurrency) while we collect traces.
